c.tagline: Ancient Silk Road capital of the Terracotta Army, city walls, and dumpling feasts.

taxi.fareNote: Cabs are metered and cheap, but drivers rarely speak English and foreign cards aren't accepted; pay cash or use Didi (linkable to Alipay/WeChat) and have your destination written in Chinese.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police, 120 for ambulance/medical, and 119 for fire. English-speaking operators are limited, so having your location written in Chinese helps.

avoid.reason: Watch for tea-house and 'art student' scams around the Bell Tower and Muslim Quarter, unlicensed taxis at the railway stations, and touts selling fake Terracotta Army tours and tickets.

hood_desc: The walled historic core around the Bell Tower, Drum Tower, and Beilin (Forest of Steles) Museum, ringed by the fully intact Ming-era City Wall; best for first-timers who want the major sights and old-city atmosphere within walking distance.

The centuries-old Hui Muslim quarter along Beiyuanmen and Huimin Jie, a maze of lantern-lit food lanes, mosques, and market stalls beside the Drum Tower; the city's top spot for street food, snacks, and evening buzz.

The Yanta district built around the Tang-dynasty Big Wild Goose Pagoda, the Datang Everbright City promenade, and the Shaanxi History Museum; a landmark-heavy area with grand plazas, fountains, and easy metro access.

An upscale, planned cultural-tourism zone south of the center around Tang Paradise and the Qujiang Pool Heritage Park, full of themed gardens, museums, and modern hotels; calmer and greener, good for a relaxed base.

Xi'an's modern business and tech belt spanning the High-tech Zone (Gaoxin) and the northern Weiyang new city, with corporate towers, malls, and international hotels; convenient and quiet but away from the historic sights.

water.note: Stick to bottled or boiled water; avoid tap water and ice made from it.

transit.hours: Metro trains run roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; buses run from early morning to around 11:00 PM, with limited late-night service.
transit.note: Xi'an Metro is a fast-growing network of 10+ lines covering the walled city, Big Wild Goose Pagoda, the high-speed rail station, and the airport (Line 14); clean, cheap, and the easiest way around, backed by an extensive city bus system.
transit.pay: Buy single-journey tokens at station machines, tap a rechargeable Chang'an Tong card, or scan the Xi'an Metro / Alipay / WeChat QR code; fares start around 2 yuan by distance. Buses cost ~2 yuan, cash or QR/card.

bus: Intercity coaches to Shaanxi towns and the Terracotta Army (Lintong)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected at restaurants, taxis, or hotels; prices are as marked and staff may even decline a tip.

food.name: Roujiamo
food.desc: Often called the Chinese hamburger: slow-braised pork or cumin-spiced beef and lamb chopped and packed into a crisp baked mo flatbread.

places.name: Fan Ji La Zhi Roujiamo
places.note: Famous braised-pork roujiamo shop; expect a queue at lunchtime.

places.name: Lao Sun Jia
places.area: Dongmutou Shi, near the Bell Tower
places.note: Time-honoured Shaanxi restaurant, a safe sit-down version with an English menu.

places.name: Beiyuanmen Muslim Street
places.note: Halal beef and lamb roujiamo stalls the whole length of the street.

food.name: Biangbiang noodles
food.desc: Belt-wide hand-slapped wheat noodles, three or four to a bowl, dressed with chilli powder, garlic and vinegar under a splash of sizzling hot oil.

places.name: Yongxingfang Food Street
places.note: Government-curated Shaanxi food street with several dedicated noodle stalls.

places.name: Fanji noodle shop
places.note: Local favourite for wide hand-pulled noodles with youpo chilli oil.

places.name: Muslim Quarter noodle houses
places.note: Dozens of small halal noodle rooms; look for the one-metre noodle sign.

food.name: Yangrou paomo
food.desc: You tear a flatbread into pea-sized crumbs yourself, then it comes back drowned in ten-hour mutton broth with glass noodles, pickled garlic and chilli.

places.name: Lao Sun Jia
places.area: Dongmutou Shi, near the Bell Tower
places.note: Founded 1898 and the most cited paomo house in the city.

places.name: Tong Sheng Xiang
places.note: The other historic paomo institution; central and used to visitors.

places.name: Yongxingfang Food Street
places.note: Several paomo counters here if the classics have a queue out the door.

food.name: Liangpi
food.desc: Cold, slippery sheets of steamed wheat or rice starch cut into ribbons with gluten cubes, cucumber, sesame paste, vinegar, garlic and chilli oil.

places.name: Wei Jia Liangpi
places.note: Long-running liangpi counter locals queue at, especially in summer.

places.name: Qinzhen liangpi stalls
places.note: Qinzhen-style rice liangpi, softer and more delicate than the wheat version.

places.name: Sajinqiao night market
places.note: Local evening street market; liangpi, rou jia mo and skewers away from the tourists.

food.name: Guantang baozi and lamb skewers
food.desc: Soup-filled steamed buns of beef or lamb with ginger, eaten with vinegar, alongside cumin-and-chilli mutton skewers grilled over coals.

places.name: Jia San Guan Tang Bao Zi
places.note: The best-known soup-dumpling house in the quarter; several floors, always busy.

places.name: Beiyuanmen Muslim Street
places.note: Continuous line of skewer grills and bun steamers from late afternoon.

places.name: Sajinqiao night market
places.note: Cheaper, more local skewer scene with high turnover and fresh charcoal.

food.name: Hulutou paomo
food.desc: Xi'an's other paomo: torn bread soaked in a clear, peppery broth with meticulously cleaned braised pork intestine, rich but not heavy.

places.name: Chunfasheng
places.note: The century-old hulutou specialist; the reference version of the dish.

places.name: Yongxingfang Food Street
places.note: Hulutou counter here for a tidier, more visitor-friendly introduction.

places.name: Sajinqiao night market
places.note: Small local shops around the market serve hulutou from early morning.

food.name: Bingfeng soda
food.desc: Xi'an's own cloudy orange soda, made in the city since 1953 and drunk ice-cold from a glass bottle to cut the chilli oil.

places.name: Beiyuanmen Muslim Street
places.note: Every stall keeps crates on ice; the standard partner to roujiamo.

places.name: Yongxingfang Food Street
places.note: Sold across the food street, including the glass-bottle nostalgia version.

places.name: Lao Sun Jia
places.area: Dongmutou Shi, near the Bell Tower

food.name: Jiangmi jiu (sweet rice wine)
food.desc: Barely alcoholic fermented glutinous rice drink served warm with osmanthus and egg drop, or chilled in summer; sweet, cloudy and comforting.

places.name: Beiyuanmen Muslim Street
places.note: Stalls ladle it hot from copper pots on cold evenings.

places.name: Yongxingfang Food Street
places.note: Served alongside the Shaanxi snack stalls; good with sweet persimmon cakes.

places.name: Sajinqiao night market

landmarks: Terracotta Army
Thousands of life-size clay warriors guard Emperor Qin Shi Huang's tomb, an astonishing archaeological wonder every traveler to China must witness once.
Xi'an City Wall
Cycle a full 14-kilometer circuit atop the best-preserved ancient city wall in China, a Ming-dynasty rampart wide enough for chariots.
Big Wild Goose Pagoda (Dayan Ta)
A 7th-century brick pagoda built to house Buddhist scriptures carried from India by monk Xuanzang, framed by fountains and Tang-style gardens.
Muslim Quarter
A lantern-lit maze of Hui food stalls sizzling with lamb skewers, biangbiang noodles and persimmon cakes behind the Drum Tower.
Bell Tower
The gilded Ming-dynasty timber tower marks Xi'an's exact center, glowing gold at night above the swirl of downtown traffic.
Drum Tower
Twin to the Bell Tower, this 1380 landmark holds ranks of giant ceremonial drums and stages short traditional music performances daily.
Great Mosque of Xi'an
One of China's oldest mosques, a tranquil fusion of Chinese pavilions and Islamic calligraphy hidden in the Muslim Quarter's winding lanes.
Shaanxi History Museum
A treasury of hundreds of thousands of artifacts—Tang gold, Zhou bronzes and tomb murals—explaining why Xi'an anchored thirteen Chinese dynasties.
Small Wild Goose Pagoda
A graceful, earthquake-cracked Tang pagoda set in peaceful gardens, paired with the free Xi'an Museum and its famous morning bell.
Huaqing Palace
Imperial hot-spring pools where Emperor Xuanzong romanced Yang Guifei, set beneath Mount Li near the site of the 1936 Xi'an Incident.

train.note: Xi'an has no international passenger trains - the nearest cross-border services are Beijing to Ulaanbaatar and Moscow, and the Urumqi to Almaty train far to the northwest, both requiring a long domestic leg first. Xi'an North handles the high-speed network: Beijing in 4.5-6 hours, Zhengzhou in about 2 hours, Chengdu in around 4 hours and Shanghai in 6-7 hours; it is 15 km north of the centre and on Metro Line 2. The older Xi'an railway station, right beside the city walls, keeps the conventional and overnight services towards Lanzhou, Urumqi and the northwest. Book on 12306 with your passport; the window opens 15 days ahead and Xi'an is a heavily booked tourist route in summer and around Chinese New Year.

bus.note: There are no international coaches from Xi'an. The Shaanxi Province Long-distance Bus Station is about 100 m south of Xi'an railway station and runs domestic services to Huashan, Luoyang, Yan'an, Taiyuan, Zhengzhou and Lanzhou, with journeys of roughly 2-12 hours. Tickets are sold at the counter with a passport rather than through an English website. For most of these destinations the high-speed train is dramatically faster, so buses are mainly useful for places off the rail network such as Huashan village stops and rural Shaanxi.

ferry.note: Xi'an is a landlocked inland city on the shallow Wei River, which carries no passenger traffic, so there are no ferry services of any kind.

half.name: Mount Hua (Huashan)
half.blurb: One of China's five sacred mountains, known for narrow cliffside plank trails and steep granite peaks.

half.name: Famen Temple
half.blurb: Buddhist temple complex housing a relic said to be a finger bone of the Buddha, discovered in a sealed underground crypt.

half.name: Qianling Mausoleum
half.blurb: Tang-dynasty imperial tomb complex of Emperor Gaozong and Empress Wu Zetian, lined with stone statues along its spirit road.
